correctness.rationale: Read frozen RESULT.md and assumptions: generator D∂xx, independent Poisson rate r=Ds², fresh i.i.d μ after every reset, calibrated D,x0. Standard renewal from Brownian hitting transform gives M_c=[1-e^{-s|x0-c|}]/[Ds²Φ_c(s)], Φ_c(s)=∫e^{-s|y-c|}μ(dy)>0 for all probabilities even without moments. On each target, positive-rate accumulation inside (0,infty) determines entire Laplace transform by holomorphic identity and folded-distance law by Laplace uniqueness. If two μ,ν have same transforms at a≠b, finite signed difference η is antisymmetric under both R_a and R_b, hence invariant under nonzero translation 2(b-a), impossible for a nonzero finite signed measure. Explicit Fourier reconstruction from cosine folds has 2x2 determinant sin(k(b-a)); discrete resonant k filled by continuity. One target only knows folded law. m finite scalar readings have m+2-point null vector including normalization with both signs. Sources 1±epsilon sin(2πny) on [0,1] at targets 0,1 have TV gap 2epsilon/pi while responses converge O(1/n) uniformly on compact positive-rate intervals (base transform stays positive). Independently checked exact finite-measurement null vector, sine transform and TV instability; unrestricted identifiability uses measure symmetry argument, not numerical inversion.

value.rationale: A sharp tomography theorem for the natural inverse resetting problem: the precise two-target threshold for arbitrary singular reset laws, with explicit insufficiency of one view, finitely many rate readings and strong TV stability. This is useful for experimental design and establishes exactly what ideal MFPT data determine.

limitations: Ideal exact positive-rate curves or sets with accumulation inside positive axis, two targets a≠b, known D and x0, independent Poisson resets and i.i.d fresh μ.
No finite-sample identification, no claim of TV stability or noisy-data estimator; arbitrarily unbounded/source-atomic μ allowed.
